summary: Round 1 critical and all three high findings are credibly closed by tech-spec changes (recall_owner_isolation.rs, expanded OAuth tests, adversarial mock proxy, stdio_backward_compat.rs). Most mediums are addressed (WASM 4 to 6, HTTP 3 to 5, MCP Inspector hardening, smithery.yaml schema validation, cargo audit). Webapp coverage remains zero (consciously deferred — acceptable for hackathon). Two genuinely new concerns surface from the round 1 fixes: (a) several of the 12 OAuth tests duplicate behavior that jsonwebtoken crate already enforces, inflating the count without proportional value, and (b) the stdio_backward_compat subprocess test has known CI flake characteristics that need pinning before merge. Test pyramid is healthy for an L hackathon MVP. Decisions 9, 10, 11 each have at least one explicit test. Verdict: improved with two minor remaining gaps and one duplicate-coverage callout — proportional to ship.

round1_critical_recall_ownership.evidence: New mcp/tests/recall_owner_isolation.rs explicitly lists cross-tenant assertion (user A cannot see user B's row) AND anonymous-401 path. Decision 9 makes the SQL filter mandatory at the function-signature level (search_attestations requires owner_pubkey parameter). Acceptance Criteria includes the matching curl-based AC line. This is a complete closure.
round1_critical_recall_ownership.remaining_concern: The integration test covers HTTP transport only. For stdio (no JWT) the spec says 'filter resolves to local-keypair pubkey'. There is no test that exercises this stdio resolution path with a multi-row DB to confirm the local-keypair pubkey actually scopes correctly. Low-severity — single-tenant by construction in stdio.

round1_high_oauth_depth.evidence: OAuth unit tests expanded from 6 to 12 with explicit list: alg=none, alg-confusion, single-use replay, tampered sub, missing state, concurrent jti, expired-code, mismatched iss/aud. All six round-1-listed gaps (a-f) are covered.

Risk-table mitigation now commits to 'Default to base64-encoded CBOR in JSON string field' — option (b) from round 1. Both halves of the round-1 fix landed.

Description matches round-1 prescription (subprocess + tools/list + sign_memory + recall round-trip). AC line 'No regressions in existing stdio MCP behavior' now has a corresponding automated test.

findings.location: Testing Strategy → Unit tests → mcp/src/oauth.rs (12 tests)
findings.issue: Some of the 12 OAuth unit tests duplicate behavior the jsonwebtoken crate already enforces by construction, inflating test count without proportional risk reduction. Specifically: (1) 'alg=none JWT submission expects 401' — jsonwebtoken's Validation::new(Algorithm::HS256) rejects alg=none by default; the test verifies library behavior, not our code. (2) 'tampered sub claim expects 401' — any byte mutation of a signed JWT fails signature check; this is testing the HMAC, not our authorization logic. (3) 'mismatched iss/aud rejection' is meaningful only if our code explicitly sets validation.set_issuer / set_audience; otherwise it tests library defaults. Litmus test: if we delete our oauth.rs claim-validation lines, do these tests still fail? For (1) and (2), only if jsonwebtoken's defaults are correctly invoked — which is one assertion, not three. The tests are not harmful, but they create maintenance load and a false sense of depth.
findings.recommendation: Keep the 12 tests but consolidate (1) and (2) into a single 'JWT validator rejects all forms of forged token (alg=none, alg-confusion HS256↔RS256, tampered signature, tampered claims)' test that asserts ONE thing: our verify_jwt() function returns Err for each of N forged inputs. This protects against accidentally calling jsonwebtoken with insecure_disable_signature_validation() or wrong Validation config — which IS our code. For iss/aud: explicitly assert our code sets validation.set_issuer(['mcp.mnemonik.xyz']) and set_audience(['mcp']) — verify the configuration line, not just library behavior. This converts library-behavior tests into our-config tests and reclaims the litmus property.

findings.issue: Subprocess-based stdio test has well-known CI flake characteristics: (1) cargo build cold-cache on CI runner can race the subprocess startup; (2) stdin/stdout buffering modes differ between local TTY and CI runners — test passes locally, fails on GitHub Actions; (3) no timeout policy specified; if the binary hangs (e.g., embedder model download in test mode), the CI job times out at the global limit (often 6h on GHA free tier) instead of a useful per-test failure; (4) no specification of how the embedder is configured for the subprocess — if it tries to download fastembed ONNX on a clean CI runner with no cache, the test takes minutes and may fail on network blips.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit guardrails to Task 7 description: (a) build the binary once with 'cargo build -p mnemonic-mcp --release' before the test (not inside the test); (b) wrap the subprocess interaction in a tokio::time::timeout(Duration::from_secs(10), ...) around each request/response pair; (c) configure the subprocess with EMBED_PROVIDER=mock or use a deterministic test embedder so the binary boots in <2s; (d) explicitly flush stdin after each write and use line-buffered reads on stdout. Without these the test will become the most-flaked test in CI within the first month and will be disabled. Listed as minor because the test exists and has the right shape — these are operational concerns, not correctness ones.

findings.location: Testing Strategy + Risks table 'webapp ↔ MCP CORS could block POST'
findings.issue: CORS configuration is called out in Decision 9 ('exact origin https://mnemonik.xyz, no Any wildcard') and Risks ('Test in CI with a request from a different origin asserting 403/CORS-rejected') but no test bullet implements this. Round 1 flagged this; round 2 retains the gap. For an OAuth flow that depends on cross-origin POST from the webapp to mcp.mnemonik.xyz, a misconfigured CORS layer is a silent demo-killer.
findings.recommendation: Add to oauth_flow.rs (or as a separate 5-line test): preflight OPTIONS /oauth/authorize with Origin: https://mnemonik.xyz returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://mnemonik.xyz; preflight with Origin: https://evil.example does NOT include that header. Total cost ~10 lines of test code; closes the round-1 low and matches the Risks-table mitigation literally.

findings.location: Acceptance Criteria 'Per-IP rate limit returns 429 after threshold' + Decision 9
findings.issue: Decision 9 introduces 3 unit tests for rate limiting (6th sign_memory → 429, 31st recall → 429, stdio bypass). The unit tests are sufficient for the limit logic itself, but no test verifies the limiter is actually wired into the /mcp router (vs. only constructed in McpState). A common bug: tower_governor layer is created but missing from .layer() chain on the route. The unit tests would still pass because they test the limiter directly; the integration would silently allow unlimited traffic.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) make the rate-limit tests integration tests against the actual Axum router (POST /mcp 6 times in a loop, assert 6th returns 429), OR (b) add a single integration test 'rate_limit_wired.rs' that fires 31 recall calls through the full HTTP stack and asserts 429 on the 31st. Option (b) is ~20 lines. The existing 3 'unit' tests can stay — but at least one must hit the real router.

findings.location: Decision 10 OAuth signed-challenge contents — replay/staleness window
findings.issue: Decision 10 specifies the challenge format blake3(state || client_id || redirect_uri || code_challenge || nonce) with 60s expiry stored keyed by state. The 12 OAuth tests cover 'expired-code rejection (TTL 60s)' which likely refers to the authorization code TTL after issuance. The /authorize challenge itself (pre-signature, 60s window per Decision 10) is a separate timer. There is no explicit test that a challenge presented after the 60s window for state binding is rejected. Under load or slow signing (e.g., user opens webapp, gets distracted, signs 90s later), this is a real path.
findings.recommendation: Add one test to the OAuth unit suite: 'challenge presented at /authorize after Decision-10 60s TTL is rejected with state_expired'. Either as a 13th test or by parameterizing the existing expired-code test to cover both timers. Use a mockable clock (mock_instant or similar) so the test runs in milliseconds.

findings.location: Testing Strategy → Manual smoke tests (4 numbered steps)
findings.issue: Round 1 medium remains: smoke checklist text in tech-spec lacks per-step Expected/Recovery/ETA structure; Task 8 description still says 'exhaustive manual flow' without committing to the tuple format. Verify-user line for Task 8 says a non-author teammate executes 'without ambiguity' — good intent but unenforceable without the format. Also, no step explicitly covers stdio backward-compat (covered automatically by stdio_backward_compat.rs now, so this part is closed).
findings.recommendation: In Task 8 description, add one sentence: 'Each step is structured as (Action, Expected output verbatim, Failure recovery, ETA in seconds)'. This is documentation guidance, not test code; ~30 seconds to add to the spec. Closes the round-1 medium proportionally.

litmusTest.notes: 4 OAuth tests (alg=none, alg-confusion, tampered-sub, tampered-claims) test library behavior more than our code — would still pass if our oauth.rs validation lines were a single Validation::new(HS256) call. Recommendation: consolidate or rewrite to assert config, not library defaults.
